text: Abstract: We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output. The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable.
label: Research Paper

text: In this work, we present an empirical investigation into deep convolutional neural networks for large-scale image recognition. Our primary contribution is a thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth using an architecture with very small (3x3) convolution filters, which shows that a significant improvement on the prior-art configurations can be achieved by pushing the depth to 16–19 weight layers.
label: Research Paper

text: We investigate unsupervised representation learning with deep contrastive methods. Our framework simplifies recently proposed contrastive self-supervised learning algorithms without requiring specialized architectures nor a memory bank. We introduce a stochastic data augmentation module and a learnable non-linear transformation between the representation and the contrastive loss function.
label: Research Paper

text: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for training stochastic gradient descent with adaptive momentum and learning rate scheduling. We demonstrate through extensive benchmarking on ImageNet and GLUE datasets that our technique accelerates convergence while avoiding catastrophic forgetting in transfer learning tasks.
label: Research Paper

text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trial outcomes for mRNA-based vaccine candidates. We analyzed randomized controlled trials published between 2020 and 2024 evaluating immunogenicity, efficacy, and adverse reaction rates across diverse demographic cohorts.

text: Quantum annealing versus gate-based quantum computation for combinatorial optimization problems. We benchmark simulated quantum annealing against classical heuristic baselines across max-cut and traveling salesperson graph instances, documenting phase transitions and scaling limits.
